subject: gk
question: Which of the following is the most abundant mineral in our body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calcium (Ca):**

 
 
• Atomic Number: 20 (meaning it has 20 protons in its nucleus).
 
• Atomic Mass: Approximately 40.08 amu (atomic mass units).
 
• Electronic Configuration: [Ar] 4s² (meaning its outermost shell has 2 electrons).
 
• Role in the Body: Crucial for bone and teeth formation, muscle contraction, nerve transmission, and blood clotting.
 
• Dietary Sources: Dairy products, leafy green vegetables, fortified foods.
 
• Deficiency: Can lead to osteoporosis, muscle cramps, and other health issues.
 
• Symbol: Ca
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phosphorus (P):**

 
 
• Atomic Number: 15 (15 protons in its nucleus).
 
• Atomic Mass: Approximately 30.97 amu.
 
• Electronic Configuration: [Ne] 3s² 3p³ (5 electrons in its outermost shell).
 
• Role in the Body: Essential for bone and teeth formation, energy production (ATP), DNA and RNA synthesis.
 
• Dietary Sources: Meat, poultry, fish, dairy, legumes, nuts.
 
• Deficiency: Can cause weakness, fatigue, bone pain, and impaired growth.
 
• Symbol: P
 
 
 
• **Iron (Fe):**
 
 
• Atomic Number: 26 (26 protons).
 
• Atomic Mass: Approximately 55.85 amu.
 
• Electronic Configuration: [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s² (8 electrons in its outermost shells).
 
• Role in the Body: Key component of hemoglobin (oxygen transport in red blood cells) and myoglobin (oxygen storage in muscles).
 
• Dietary Sources: Red meat, leafy green vegetables, beans, fortified cereals.
 
• Deficiency: Leads to iron-deficiency anemia, characterized by fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath.
 
• Symbol: Fe
 
 
 
• **Copper (Cu):**
 
 
• Atomic Number: 29 (29 protons).
 
• Atomic Mass: Approximately 63.55 amu.
 
• Electronic Configuration: [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ (11 electrons in its outermost shells).
 
• Role in the Body: Involved in various enzyme reactions, including energy production, iron metabolism, and neurotransmitter synthesis. Also important for immune function.
 
• Dietary Sources: Seafood, nuts, seeds, legumes, organ meats.
 
• Deficiency: Can cause anemia, fatigue, neurological problems, and impaired immune function.
 
• Symbol: Cu
 
 

6d
